name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,260

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Proceeding by inquiry, one breaks into variable French also, or the like

indicators.note: something that breaks into a thing ends up lodged inside it, so the single letter goes within the last chunk

blocks.note: z is a standard algebraic variable
et is French for 'and', i.e. also
etc, et cetera, means 'and the like'
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone investigating a French phrase meets a variable that sneaks in among the words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French also' is a stretch: et means 'and', standing for also here.
explanation.definitionFit: Zetetic is a rare adjective for investigating or seeking, from the Greek verb for searching out.

clue.text: Informal apology for flipping about men wearing furs

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it end to end, so the apology is read backwards
about means going round, so the turned apology wraps round the next pair of pieces

blocks.note: soz is British slang for 'sorry'
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
dressed in something is wearing it

explanation.surface: Someone offers a casual sorry after cursing at men dressed in fur coats.
explanation.walkthrough: ZOS is split as Z...OS around ORIN to give ZORINOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Zorinos are pelts of South American skunks, traded under that name as a type of skin.

clue.text: Sees races with bets one might dash off on the hoof?

definitions.text: one might dash off on the hoof?

indicators.note: letters that race about are running wild, so the two words are mixed up together

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler watches the horse races and places wagers, with a hint of hooves running off.
explanation.walkthrough: The racecourse surface makes the hoofed runner seem to be a horse; it is an African antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsessebe is a fast African antelope, a hoofed animal that could well run off at speed.

clue.text: Rum form of motor sport for American serving up in northern forests

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
one thing for another means swapping it in in place of the other

blocks.note: F1, Formula One, written with the digit as the letter I
a GI is a serving US soldier
taiga is the coniferous forest of the far north

explanation.surface: An odd sort of motor racing for a US soldier stationed in the northern woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the adjective meaning odd, but it is the drink. The swap happens on the reversed soldier inside the forest word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tafia is a cheap West Indian spirit distilled from molasses, a kind of the liquor called rum.

clue.text: Prayer — and possible dish of duck eggs — offered up

indicators.note: in a down clue something offered up is lifted bottom to top, so the eggs are read upwards

blocks.note: duck confit is a classic French dish of preserved duck
roe is fish eggs

explanation.surface: A prayer is said, and a dinner of duck and eggs is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offered up' suits a prayer in the surface, but it turns ROE upside down to give EOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Confiteor is the Latin prayer of confession in the Catholic Mass, beginning 'I confess'.

clue.text: Lots of swinging in gym — after crash, I would add

indicators.note: after places the addition behind the first piece, setting the order of the two parts

blocks.note: to crash is to sleep, and a kip is a sleep in British slang
a PS, postscript, is what a letter writer adds

explanation.surface: After a fall in the gym someone wants to add a remark about all the swinging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash' suggests a fall from the apparatus; here it means a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A kip is a gymnastic movement swinging the legs to rise onto a bar, so the plural is several such swings.

clue.text: Onager to eliminate one at château walls last, releasing stone

indicators.note: walls surround what they enclose, so the French word goes round what follows
releasing lets something go, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: a KO, knockout, eliminates a fighter
un is French for one
taken as written
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A wild ass is to be removed from a French castle, its walls left free of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At château' just signals that the French word for one is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The koulan, or kulan, is the wild ass of central Asia, an alternative name for the onager.

clue.text: German silver medallist’s final round no good, with stuff said previously

indicators.note: final points to the closing letter of the medallist
said means the word is spoken, so its sound is spelt differently
previously puts this piece before the others in the answer

blocks.note: to stuff is to pack, here spelt another way with the same sound
the last letter of medallist
O is round in shape
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A German silver medallist has a bad last round after earlier talk of stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German silver' looks like the medal in the surface; it is the definition, a nickel alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paktong is a Chinese white alloy of copper, nickel and zinc, the metal also called nickel or German silver.

clue.text: In need of cheering up, chap gets letter

blocks.note: someone sad needs cheering up
a chap is a he

explanation.surface: A gloomy man receives a letter in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests mail; it is an alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadhe is a character of the Hebrew alphabet, the eighteenth, also spelt tsade.

clue.text: Aberdeen’s extravagant display in cup’s ending with a draw

indicators.note: ending points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the last letter of cup
taken as written
a raffle is a prize draw

explanation.surface: Aberdeen's football team puts on a big show as a cup tie ends in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests a tied match; here it is a lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffle is a Scots word for an ostentatious show, so it is labelled as northern speech by the city.

clue.text: Lots of strange sensations affecting hearing after two more strokes

indicators.note: after two more strokes asks for the final letter to be redrawn, changing it into another

blocks.note: aural means relating to the ear
an L drawn with two extra horizontal strokes becomes an E

explanation.surface: Someone feels odd sensations in the ears after a couple of further strokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strokes' suggests medical attacks; they are pen strokes added to the L of AURAL, turning it into E.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a strange warning feeling before a migraine or seizure; aurae is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Female duck seen flapping getting pulled from boggy ground by poet

definitions.text: pulled from boggy ground by poet

indicators.note: something flapping is thrown about in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A female duck is spotted flapping as it is hauled out of a marsh by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is Shakespeare, whose King Lear speaks of fogs that are fen-sucked.
explanation.definitionFit: Fen-sucked means drawn up out of marshes, a Shakespearean coinage for vapours rising from swamps.

clue.text: Failing in recognition of some liaison, gamely retreating

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them
retreating goes backwards, so the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: An affair, bravely conducted, ends in a failure to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnosia is a medical disorder in which a patient cannot identify objects, people or sounds despite intact senses.

clue.text: Shows great impatience close to lecture, making academic start

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: someone who is agog is eagerly impatient, so 'is agog'
the last letter of lecture

explanation.surface: A student grows restless near the end of a lecture as term begins.
explanation.definitionFit: An isagoge is a scholarly introduction to a subject, the opening of an academic study.

clue.text: America’s to move to block newspaper: a particular one in New York

definitions.text: a particular one in New York

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in its way, here inside the newspaper

blocks.note: the FT, Financial Times, is a British newspaper
US's, America's, spelt without the apostrophe
to budge is to move

explanation.surface: The US sets out to obstruct a newspaper, one particular title in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' looks like 'specific'; it means fussy, and the phrase is American.
explanation.definitionFit: A fussbudget is American slang for a fussy, finicky person who complains about small details.

clue.text: Skin condition got from horse he passed on in Washington hotel

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the city's abbreviation

blocks.note: DC, District of Columbia, is the city's designation
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
obiit is Latin for 'he died', seen on tombstones
H is Hotel in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A rash caught from a horse at a hotel in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhobi itch is a tropical fungal rash once blamed on clothes washed by Indian laundrymen, called dhobis.

clue.text: Trail to the west following a band of Bedouins

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading leftwards
following puts this piece after the article

blocks.note: taken as written
to trail behind is to lag

explanation.surface: A desert track heads west behind a group of nomads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a group of tribesmen; it is a headband.
explanation.definitionFit: An agal is the cord worn by Arab men round the head to hold the headcloth in place.

clue.text: With large supply key, however small flask appears

indicators.note: read as supple-y, something bendy and flexible, so the word is reshaped

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
taken as written
tho is an informal spelling of though, meaning however
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Despite a big supply of something essential, only a small bottle turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as a noun after 'large'; it is the adverb from supple, flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: A lekythos was an ancient Greek narrow-necked oil jar, a slender vessel for oils and perfume.

clue.text: What emerges after laying into young tough encouraged nag?

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a Ted, Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth gang member
a chick hatches out of an egg once it has been laid

explanation.surface: A young thug gets laid into by something emerging, and a horse is urged on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laying into' suggests attacking; the egg-laying leads to a hatchling.
explanation.definitionFit: To tchick is to make a clicking sound with the tongue, as riders do to urge a horse on.

clue.text: US hospital department needing sort of radiation area with licence

blocks.note: ER, emergency room, is the American casualty department
UV, ultraviolet, is a type of radiation

explanation.surface: An American emergency ward needs a certain kind of radiation zone that is licensed.
explanation.definitionFit: An eruv is a boundary area within which observant Jews are permitted to carry things on the Sabbath.

clue.text: Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race maybe involving British pair with only hair between them

definitions.text: pair with only hair between them

indicators.note: something involving another wraps it up within itself

blocks.note: the Boat Race is a rowing race between universities, a uni row
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: The university Boat Race features a British pair whose rivalry is only a hair's breadth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes two eyebrows joined by hair over the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A unibrow is a single continuous line of eyebrow, the two brows linked across the bridge of the nose.

clue.text: Honey-eater 70 minutes late for his teatime in Grantchester?

definitions.text: 70 minutes late for his teatime in Grantchester?

blocks.note: first meaning: an Australian bird of the honeyeater family

blocks.clueFragment: 70 minutes late for his teatime in Grantchester?
blocks.note: second meaning: the hour reached by adding seventy minutes to ten to three

explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Brooke's poem The Old Vicarage, Grantchester ends: 'Stands the Church clock at ten to three? And is there honey still for tea?' Seventy minutes after ten to three is four.
explanation.definitionFit: The four-o'clock is an Australian friarbird, a honeyeater named for its call, and it is also simply the time.

clue.text: Investigative procedure soon replacing the years of excess

indicators.note: replacing means one piece takes the place of another inside a word

blocks.note: an orgy is a bout of excess
Y is the abbreviation for years
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: An inquiry will soon take the place of years of indulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: ANON replaces the Y of ORGY.
explanation.definitionFit: An organon is a system of logical rules for investigation, after the title of Aristotle's logical works.

clue.text: Misfortune suffered when ace and I swapped around hunting game once

indicators.note: swapped around means the two named letters trade places

blocks.note: one who suffered misfortune ill had it
A is ace on playing cards
taken as written

explanation.surface: A run of bad luck as a card player's ace changes hands during an old hunting game.
explanation.walkthrough: In ILL HAD the I and the A trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: All-hid was an old name for hide-and-seek, the children's game of hunting for concealed players.

clue.text: Judge excellent, in the manner of one Basque game

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
A1 means excellent, with the 1 written as I
à la means in the style of
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A judge rates one Basque sport excellent in its style.
explanation.definitionFit: Jai alai is the fast court sport from the Basque Country, played with a curved basket, also called pelota.

clue.text: Ruffle, and shut up, following quick blow

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the word from the bottom
following places this piece after the blow

blocks.note: a jab is a quick punch
a door pushed to is shut

explanation.surface: Someone is ruffled and told to shut up after a sharp punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as 'be quiet'; 'up' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A jabot is a frill or ruffle of lace worn at the neck, on a shirt front.

clue.text: Singer adopting tongue, abandoning old, native one

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the bird surrounds what follows
abandoning means leaving behind, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a tit is a songbird
lingo is slang for a language or tongue
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A singer learns a local language and drops an old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a vocalist; it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tlingit are an indigenous people of south-east Alaska and British Columbia, so a member is a native American.

clue.text: Car thief dropping matching keys and brace

indicators.note: dropping means letting go, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a twoccer is British slang for a car thief, from TWOC, taking without owner's consent
C is a musical key, and a matching pair is two of them

explanation.surface: A car thief drops a pair of identical keys along with a support bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keys' suggests car keys; they are musical keys, two Cs.
explanation.definitionFit: A twoer is anything counting as two, and a brace means a pair of things, such as game birds.

clue.text: Italian town hospital within reach, after short drag

indicators.note: within places the hospital inside the phrase for reach
short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter
after places the town's later part behind the shortened word

blocks.note: a drag is something tedious, a bore
to reach a place is to get to it
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An Italian town's hospital is easy to reach after a short slog.
explanation.walkthrough: BORE loses its E; H goes inside GET TO to give GHETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A borghetto is Italian for a small town or hamlet, a little borgo; several Italian places bear the name.

clue.text: I finally sneak back around noon bringing cheese for delivery

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word sneak
back means the pieces are read in the opposite direction
around means going round the noon letter

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the last letter of sneak
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Someone finally slips back home at midday with cheese for a delivery round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a parcel round; it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken-no is a Scottish cheese made secretly for the women attending a birth, eaten to celebrate a new baby.

clue.text: Wife less to the fore in rough stuff no longer beat kid?

indicators.note: the wife's letter is to stand less far forward, so it shifts back a place and the word is rearranged

blocks.note: tweed is a rough woollen cloth, and W is the usual abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife in a tough situation no longer hits a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is goatskin leather, and the definition is obsolete, hence 'no longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tew was an old verb for working leather by beating, so kidskin was once tewed into shape.

clue.text: What can aid circulation of choir round piano every so often?

indicators.note: every so often takes letters at intervals, here every second one

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A choir walks round a piano, which helps something circulate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulation' suggests moving around the room; it is blood flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirudin is the anticoagulant in leech saliva, used medically to stop blood clotting and keep it flowing.
